itens.titulo: China’s CXMT and Broadcom’s CEO Rattle Chip Stocks: Which Fear Matters More for Micron?
itens.descricao: China’s CXMT and Broadcom’s CEO Rattle Chip Stocks: Which Fear Matters More for Micron? Yahoo Finance
trechos: The chip selloff rolled into a second day on Tuesday, October 13.
Micron (MU:NASDAQ) was down about 4.5% by 10 a.m.
ET, after a 3.9% drop on Monday.
Nvidia (NVDA:NASDAQ) and Broadcom (AVGO:NASDAQ) each slipped about 1% before the bell, Forbes reported.
Asia took the worst of it overnight: SK Hynix fell 10.1% and Samsung 7.4%.
Research firm TrendForce, cited by Forbes, estimates the design could pack 30% to 50% more memory into the same chip area.
SSpeaking in Singapore on Monday, Broadcom CEO Hock Tan said "a lot of investors have no clue what they are investing in," and compared AI investing to a casino.

TIKR's data shows Micron's gross margin climbing from 37.72% in the quarter ended May 2025 to 86.76% in the quarter ended September 2026, a 49-point jump in five quarters, driven by tight supply of AI server memory.

itens.titulo: Jamie Dimon says JPMorgan Chase is putting up gates to protect against 'rogue agents'
itens.descricao: Jamie Dimon says JPMorgan Chase is putting up gates to protect against 'rogue agents' Yahoo Finance UK
trechos: - Jamie Dimon said that the bank will protect against "rogue agents" by keeping most out.

The typical security concerns around any new adaptation of technology are "heightened" with AI agents, "because you don't want rogue agents, and there could be thousands of them," JPMorgan Chase CEO Dimon said during an earnings call Tuesday.
"In the meantime, we're not going to allow just any outside agent to come in inside the company because that's just too risky for clients and for JPMorgan," Dimon said.
The bank is already blocking access to "to the extent that we're able to block those," Jeremy Barnum, the bank's chief financial officer, said.
"I think right now, some of the services that offer that do it through credential sharing, and we have a long record of being against that way of doing things, screen scraping, et cetera," he said.
"It's not secure." If a customer gives an AI agent their credentials, they could be responsible for any unwanted actions the agent takes.
"It's not an ideal state of things," Barnum said.

Bank stocks, already declining following bond market turmoil, have fallen further since the launch of Meta's Muse on September 22, and Barnum said they saw "a little bit of a response in bank stocks around those releases."

itens.titulo: Coherent Stock Falls Nearly 8% as Ciena and Lumentum Drop About 10%. Here’s Where the Stock Could Go by 2031
itens.descricao: Coherent Stock Falls Nearly 8% as Ciena and Lumentum Drop About 10%. Here’s Where the Stock Could Go by 2031 Yahoo Finance
trechos: Key Stats for Coherent Stock - Current Price: $288.02 - Target Price (Mid): ~$1,130 - Street Target: ~$413 - Potential Total Return: ~294% - Annualized IRR: ~34% / year What Happened?
Coherent (COHR:NYSE) closed at $288.02 on October 12, down 7.87%, as optical stocks sold off together.
Ciena (CIEN) fell 9.95%, and Lumentum (LITE) fell 9.78% in the same session.

Operating Cash Flow Missed All Five In the June quarter, the fiscal fourth quarter of 2026, revenue of $2,045.50 million beat the Street by 3.26%, according to Coherent's fourth-quarter results and investor relations materials.
Operating cash flow came in at $69.46 million against $374.10 million expected.
For the full fiscal year, GAAP net income reached $769.90 million, while operating cash flow was only $79.51 million.
Capex then widened it: the June quarter's $555.68 million ran 88% above the Street's $295.57 million estimate.
Fiscal 2026 free cash flow reached negative $1.02 billion, and net debt ended the year at $2.06 billion, or 1.21 times EBITDA.

itens.titulo: The 10-year Treasury yield falls as energy prices stabilize
itens.descricao: The 10-year Treasury yield falls as energy prices stabilize CNBC
trechos: The 10-year Treasury note yield fell on Tuesday after energy prices stabilized, as investors looked ahead to key economic data releases this week, including the latest U.S.
The yield on the 10-year Treasury note — the main benchmark for mortgages, auto loans, and credit card debt — fell more than 1 basis point to 5.229%.
Treasury yield — which tend to move on geopolitical events — was down more than 2 basis points at 5.574%.
The yield on the 2-year Treasury note, which more closely follows short-term Federal Reserve rate decisions, rose more than 2 basis points to 4.812%.
One basis point equals 0.01%, or 1/100th of 1%, and yields and prices move inversely.
Brent crude futures were down 0.8% at $105.83 a barrel.
WTI futures rose 0.2% to $93.92 per barrel.
September's annual inflation rate — due out Wednesday — is expected to come in at 3.7%, according to consensus forecasts, up from August's 3.4% print.
